items.title: UK's Prince William to be joined by wife Kate for visit to India
items.summary: MUMBAI/LONDON: Kate, Britain's Princess of Wales, will undertake her biggest foreign trip since having treatment for cancer when she joins her husband Prince William in India for his annual Earthshot Prize awards this week. Heir-to-the-throne William, 44, and Kate are flying out for a series of events across Mumbai during a three-day visit that includes Tuesday's awards ceremony. William and Kate will also attend events linked to Indian cricket, fashion and cinema.

items.title: Golf-crazy Trump to appeal ruling keeping Washington park open
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump criticised a judge's ruling that a park in the heart of Washington must remain open to the public, after his administration sought to close it for a golf course renovation. An avid golfer who owns courses around the world, Trump aims to turn Washington's East Potomac Golf Links, a public course with affordable rates, into a facility capable of hosting major championship-calibre events. Trump wrote on Truth Social.

items.title: Those in high office must remain open to questioning, says Anwar
items.summary: MANILA: Those holding high office must remain open to questioning, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said, as he highlighted the importance of parliamentary independence and reforms to the legislature's administration. He said the Parliamentary Services Act represented a substantial reform, as it involved the executive relinquishing administrative powers over Parliament to the House and its Speaker. Also present were Anwar's wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony.

items.title: US air travel disruptions to persist until late on Sunday
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US air travel is not expected to return to normal schedules until late on Sunday, the head of the FAA said, as the aviation system gradually recovers from a nationwide flight shutdown that officials blamed on routine maintenance gone awry. That followed about 9,200 flights cancelled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications. FlightAware said 875 flights scheduled for Sunday were already cancelled.

items.title: 'Inside Gaza': Reporting a war when it hits home
items.summary: That's the issue explored in Inside Gaza, a new documentary that follows journalists from global news agency AFP who were trapped in the territory as Israel exacted a fearsome revenge for Hamas' Oct 7 attack. "Palestinian journalists could not do that. Israel almost immediately sealed the borders of the Gaza Strip and barred international journalists from entering.

items.title: World on cusp of lethal autonomous weapons revolution
items.summary: Lethal autonomous weapons powered by artificial intelligence (AI) are set to revolutionise warfare, but there is no proper regulatory or legal framework governing the new technology. Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) "can identify, select and engage a target without the intervention of a human operator in the execution of these tasks", said Geneva Centre for Security Policy head of global and emerging risks Jean-Marc Rickli. Autonomous weapons have long existed.

items.title: Heritage building gutted in fire in Melaka
items.summary: MELAKA: A heritage building along Jalan Laksamana was gutted in a fire this evening, alarming visitors in the popular tourist area. Buletin TV3 reported that the affected premises were about 150 metres from an iconic historic square within the Unesco World Heritage Site. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: NST Leader: Coalition-building is now a political necessity
items.summary: This election offers another illustration of how the political landscape has undergone considerable changes in recent years, with traditional rivalries increasingly giving way to political cooperation and coalition-building. The nation's increasingly fragmented political landscape in recent years has made such cooperation more important, even vital, for long-term national political stability. Long-term political well-being for the country demands that responsible political groupings think outside the box with the end of rigid political boundaries.

items.title: 74-year-old doctor missing while windsurfing off Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A search and rescue operation is underway for a 74-year-old doctor who went missing while windsurfing off Tanjung Bunga tonight. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the state operations centre received a distress call from a member of the public at 7.42pm. "Upon arrival, the team immediately launched a surface search operation in the waters off Tanjung Bunga," he said in a statement tonight.

items.title: US ties will not stop Malaysia from engaging China, says Anwar
items.summary: MANILA: Malaysia's relationship with the United States will not prevent it from engaging independently with other countries, including China, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said foreign investments must operate within Malaysia's national policy framework and respect the country's interests as it navigates an increasingly uncertain geopolitical environment. Also present were Anwar's wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony.

items.title: Man arrested after brandishing knife at security guards in Wisma Darul Aman
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: A man was arrested after allegedly brandishing a knife at security guards at Wisma Darul Aman here after entering the premises without stopping at the security checkpoint this morning. Kota Setar police chief Assistant Commissioner Syed Basri Syed Ali said a 29-year-old security guard who noticed the incident gave chase and stopped the suspect to ask about his presence at the premises. Syed Basri said the suspect, who was taken to Alor Setar police station for further action, was from Kampung Berjaya here.

items.title: DOE investigates two-day spike in unhealthy air quality at Batu Muda
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Environment (DOE) is investigating a rise in the Air Pollutant Index (API) at its Batu Muda Air Quality Monitoring Station here, which has recorded unhealthy readings of above 150 for the past two days. In a statement today, DOE said investigations began on Nov 14 and involved inspections of the monitoring station, field patrols and efforts to identify possible sources of air pollution in the surrounding areas. "Field patrols identified two small-scale open burning incidents, which were extinguished on the same day.

items.title: Kepong nightclub destroyed in fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An entertainment outlet in Jalan Metro Perdana Barat, Kepong, was almost completely destroyed in a fire today. Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mokhtar said firefighters from five stations and three voluntary fire brigades were deployed after receiving an emergency call at 11.23am. He said the premises owner informed the department that everyone inside had been instructed to evacuate before the fire spread.

items.title: Sanusi hopes BN-PN cooperation continues into GE16
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: The cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) should continue into the 16th General Election (GE16), following their combined success in the Melaka state election yesterday. PN and PAS central election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said he hoped the cooperation would continue, as it appeared to have received support from the majority of voters. In the 16th Melaka election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured four and PN won three.

items.title: Three Malaysians fined 12,000 baht over traffic obstruction in Hat Yai
items.summary: SONGKHLA: Three Malaysian tourists were fined a total of 12,000 baht (about RM1,447) by Thai police after they were caught obstructing traffic and making illegal vehicle modifications along Phetkasem Road in Hat Yai early today. Hat Yai Police Station deputy traffic inspector Police Lieutenant Prut Pattanapran said the three men, aged between 26 and 30, were summoned to the police station along with a Thai national following public complaints about their conduct. Prut said their actions angered local residents before footage of the incident went viral on social media.

items.title: Kedah civil servants to receive RM3,000 special aid
items.summary: ALOR SETAR: Kedah civil servants and members of the state administration will receive RM3,000 in special financial assistance in appreciation of their service and dedication. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said the assistance would benefit 5,031 recipients and be paid in three instalments in December this year, February and August next year. "In appreciation of their hard work, I am pleased to announce that the state government has approved this special financial assistance, involving a total allocation of RM15 million," he said when tabling the Kedah 2027 Budget at the Kedah State Legislative Assembly here.

items.title: From 328 to 56: Selangor flood hotspots down 82.9pc in 10 years, says MB
items.summary: KLANG, Nov 15 — The number of flood hotspots in Selangor has dropped significantly by 82.9 per cent, from 328 areas in the 2016/2017 period to just 56 locations this year, following the implementation of various mitigation measures as well as continuous improvement of the drainage system by the state government. “We will focus on the 56 identified hotspots because the efforts we have undertaken in Selangor have proven effective in reducing and addressing flooding, including in Kampung Bukit Lanchong and Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam, as well as several other areas. Also present were Ministry of Education (MOE) Daily School Management Division director Mohd Hanafi Samad and Selangor Education director Wan Nor Ashikin Abu Kassim.

items.title: Woman dies in two-car collision near Kota Tinggi after vehicle veers into oncoming traffic
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 15 — A 60-year-old woman was killed in an accident involving two cars at Kilometre 45 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Mersing near Kota Tinggi today. Kota Tinggi district police chief Supt Yusof Othman said police received information from the public about the incident at 2 pm. He said the accident involved a Toyota Vios driven by a 33-year-old man and a Proton Saga driven by a 28-year-old woman.

items.title: Zahid: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute to be resolved soon, in line with state constitution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said the dispute involving the Negeri Sembilan royal and the state administration will be resolved soon in accordance with the state constitution. “We will do whatever necessary, provided that the problems faced by the people of Negeri are resolved and that the state administration runs smoothly and operates in accordance with the state constitution.” However, the state government officially withdrew that letter yesterday, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the state constitution and customary traditions.

items.title: ‘We won big’: Sanusi wants PAS-led Perikatan-BN partnership to carry on to GE16
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Nov 15 — PAS leader Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor today said Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) should carry their partnership into the 16th general election after their win in the Melaka state election. Sanusi, who is both PN and PAS election chief, said he hoped to see that happen after seeing how the majority of voters accepted the pairing, Berita Harian reported this evening. Asked about his lighter presence on the Melaka campaign trail, Muhammad Sanusi said he had to concentrate on preparing the state budget, which required close scrutiny.

items.title: Perikatan to decide stance on Sarawak polls as BN sits out, says Annuar Musa
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will determine its stance on contesting the upcoming Sarawak state election soon, according to its Information Chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa. This follows an announcement by BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi that the coalition will not contest any seats in the 13th Sarawak state election. “BN has no intention of contesting any state seats in Sarawak, as this is the understanding between Umno and PBB in the state,” Zahid said.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Sunday, Nov 15, 2026
items.summary: Missed what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1578466]] [[nid:1578465]] [[nid:1578464]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: GRS MPs to submit memorandum to PAC, seek expanded Pan Borneo probe
items.summary: PAPAR, Nov 15 — Seven Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) Members of Parliament will submit a memorandum to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) next week seeking an expanded scope of investigation into the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, including an examination of the basis and implications of the decision to terminate the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model in 2019. Papar MP Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. their spokesman, said the move was important to ensure that the PAC investigation not only focused on the project’s current status and performance, but also examined previous policy decisions allegedly affecting its implementation schedule, contractor appointments and rising construction costs.

items.title: With MIC’s backing, BN vows to field PPP candidates in upcoming general election, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is committed to fielding candidates from the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) to represent the coalition in the upcoming 16th General Election (GE16). BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan remained steadfast alongside other coalition partners in efforts to revitalise the party as a new component member of BN. “With the agreement of Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran (MIC president) and Datuk Seri M. Saravanan (MIC deputy president), I am determined that we will field PPP candidates in the upcoming general election,” he said in his speech at the Malaysia PPP Deepavali Open House here today.

items.title: Parit Yaani crash: Johor govt to bear medical costs, provide monthly aid to orphaned siblings, says exco
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Nov 15 — The Johor government, through the Johor State Islamic Religious Council (MAINJ), will cover the medical costs, including plastic surgery, for the two orphaned siblings who survived an accident along Jalan Yong Peng-Muar, near Parit Yaani, on November 1. State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the assistance would also include a monthly allowance, as both children were orphaned following the tragedy. Elaborating, Mohd Fared said the state government was also prepared to cover other expenses should the need arise.

items.title: Voter support alone not enough to form government, says Amirudin
items.summary: KLANG: Increased voter support alone is insufficient to form a government, with cooperation between political coalitions proving to be a decisive factor, says Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. The Pakatan Harapan (PH) election director said forming a government required more than just election strategies, as political parties also needed to reach an understanding and work together with other coalitions. He said preliminary results of the Melaka state election showed positive gains in support, particularly among Malay voters and younger people.

items.title: Vehicles over 5m barred from Sibu road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28 for festive decor
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 15 — Vehicles exceeding five metres in height are prohibited from entering a designated road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28, 2027 to accommodate Christmas street lighting and festive decorations. Sibu Municipal Council (SMC) in a statement said the restriction, which took effect on November 14, applies to the road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang, behind the WTK Holdings Berhad building. Meanwhile, the council said the Sibu Christmas Celebration 2026, themed ‘Lighting Up Sibu, Celebrating Christmas Together’, aimed to bring the community together, promote cultural harmony and share the joy of the festive season.

items.title: Heavy rain floods homes in 2 Penang villages [WATCH]
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Heavy rain flooded homes and access roads in two Penang villages today, as water levels rose rapidly in low-lying areas. The affected areas were Kampung Tasik Junjung in Simpang Ampat and Kampung Sulup in Teluk Kumbar. Floodwaters also entered several homes in Kampung Sulup, Teluk Kumbar.

items.title: Senator warns early Parliament dissolution could derail Budget 2027 and force temporary spending, citing 2022 precedent
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 15 — Calls for an early dissolution of the Dewan Rakyat are ill-timed as Budget 2027 has yet to complete the parliamentary approval process, said Senator Datuk Ahmad Ibrahim. He said dissolving Parliament before the Budget was passed could disrupt the government’s financial planning and delay funding for development projects, infrastructure programmes and other public commitments. “This would require a new government and Parliament to reintroduce and approve the Budget, potentially delaying financial authorisations needed to sustain government operations and implement planned programmes.

items.title: No pressure on Anwar to dissolve Parliament, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: SEREMBAN: There is currently no pressure on Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to dissolve Parliament to pave the way for the 16th general election (GE16), says Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. He said the prime minister had his own considerations on the appropriate time to dissolve Parliament, adding that the Federal Government's current term had yet to expire and Anwar continued to enjoy majority support among members of parliament. There is no pressure to make any sudden move to dissolve Parliament.

items.title: Kedah aims to cut operating deficit to 10.59pc with RM1.34b Budget 2027, says MB
items.summary: He said the revenue target represented an increase of RM12 million from the RM838 million targeted in 2026, with land revenue contributing the largest share at RM551 million, followed by miscellaneous revenue (RM253 million), forestry revenue (RM30 million) and district revenue (RM16 million). He said RM245 million of the development allocation was set aside for the State Development Fund, involving 10 implementing departments, while RM12.53 million was allocated for forestry development. The Water Supply Development Fund received RM143.75 million, comprising RM138.75 million from federal government loans for the implementation of three loan-funded projects and RM5 million from the state government’s allocation.

items.title: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack
items.summary: AMMAN: Jordan's State Security Court sentenced three men to death on Sunday for carrying out an attack on a church in the southern governorate of Karak last month that killed nine people, the state news agency Petra reported. Authorities said 34 people were also wounded. Syrian authorities said seven people, including three children and a woman, were killed.

items.title: BN to skip Sarawak state polls under Umno-PBB understanding, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will not contest any seats in the 13th Sarawak state election, its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. The decision is in line with an understanding between Umno and Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Ahmad Zahid, who is also Umno president, said. Also present were PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan and MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.

items.title: ‘Do not be alarmed’: MetMalaysia to conduct tsunami warning siren test in Kudat tomorrow
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Nov 15 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) will conduct a siren test for the Malaysian Tsunami Early Warning System (SAATNM) at the Kudat District Police Headquarters (IPD) tomorrow. In a post on Facebook, MetMalaysia said the test is scheduled to take place between 9 am and noon. “MetMalaysia will provide updates should there be any changes,” the statement read.

items.title: Health Ministry targets full capacity at Pasir Gudang Hospital
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Health Ministry will prioritise efforts to bring Pasir Gudang Hospital in Johor to full operational capacity, from its current level of 85 per cent. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was implementing an aggressive plan to fill vacant positions to ensure the hospital could operate at full capacity, with 304 beds and 16 delivery rooms. "Our current operational level is 85 per cent.

items.title: Ageing 40-year-old water tank bursts in Kuala Kangsar, affecting 520 consumers; no damage or injuries reported
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 15 — The bursting of a 455-cubic-metre water tank at Taman Kuala Kangsar in Kuala Kangsar yesterday was caused by the condition of its structure, which was more than 40 years old. Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Public Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the Kuala Kangsar operations centre of the Perak Water Board (LAP) received information about the incident at about 5pm, which affected water supply to approximately 520 consumers in the surrounding areas. He said LAP had carried out washing and cleaning works on roads around the burst Taman Kuala Kangsar tank, while direct water supply through the main pipeline to the affected areas, namely Taman Kuala Kangsar and Taman Meranti, had also been implemented.

items.title: 40-year-old structure caused Kuala Kangsar water tank burst
items.summary: Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Public Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the Perak Water Board's (LAP) Kuala Kangsar operations centre received information about the incident about 5pm. The incident affected water supply to about 520 consumers in the surrounding areas. He said LAP had carried out cleaning works on roads around the damaged tank, while direct water supply through the main pipeline had been provided to the affected areas of Taman Kuala Kangsar and Taman Meranti.

items.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left company in August 2025
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Megaspeed said on Sunday that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised US national security concerns, had officially left Megaspeed on Aug 30, 2025, and had no current role at the Singapore-based company. On Friday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that four government agencies favoured putting Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, on a trade black list but not the Commerce Department that was in charge. Bessent said Treasury, Pentagon, the State Department and the US Trade Representative's Office had favoured adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department entity list for months.

items.title: Selangor flood evacuees fall to 1,399; Perak down to 191
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak declined as of 4pm today. In SELANGOR, 1,399 people from 370 families were still taking shelter at six relief centres in Kuala Selangor, down from 1,493 people from 398 families this morning. In PERAK, the number of evacuees also fell to 191 people from 58 families, compared with 293 people from 85 families this morning.

items.title: BN plans to field PPP candidates in next general election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional plans to field People's Progressive Party candidates in the next general election, subject to agreement from MIC's top leadership. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the plan would require the agreement of MIC president Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran and deputy president Datuk Seri M Saravanan. Zahid said he respected PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan for keeping the party in BN.

items.title: Nearly 1,500 migrants arrive in Canary Islands in one day
items.summary: MADRID: Almost 1,500 migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands on Saturday, the highest number in a single day since 2020, the EFE news agency reported on Sunday, citing the maritime rescue service. The previous one-day record was the 1,461 people rescued in waters off the Canary Islands on Nov 7, 2020, maritime rescue services said on Sunday. The rescued migrants were taken to El Hierro, one of the smallest Canary Islands.

items.title: Indonesia was frank on steps taken over forest fires, Asean chair says
items.summary: On Friday, a study said thousands of hectares of land on palm oil and pulpwood concessions run by large listed firms were burnt during Indonesia's worst fire season in years, highlighting the role of deforestation and land clearing. Another report quoting scientists said, wildfires that hit large parts of Indonesia from August to October and plunged much of Southeast Asia into hazardous smoke were made much worse by "record-breaking" heat caused by human-induced climate change. While a very strong El Nino was the dominant factor in determining the extremely low levels of rainfall across Indonesia from July, human-induced climate change contributed around 1.6 degrees Celsius of additional heat during the fire season, said a report by climate research group World Weather Attribution.

items.title: 1,606 flood victims remain at relief centres in 3 states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,606 flood victims from 432 families remained at nine temporary relief centres in Selangor, Perak and Sarawak as of 4.30pm. The Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal recorded the highest number of evacuees in Selangor, with 1,408 people from 373 families housed at seven centres in Kuala Selangor. In Perak, 191 people from 58 families were staying at two centres in Hilir Perak.

items.title: Buried under hot tar, 11-year-old Hasya Fahira needs surgery
items.summary: Johor Islamic Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Khalid said specialists from Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) would be brought to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) to perform the procedure, sparing the girl, Hasya Fahira Zulkifli, from having to be transferred. He said her injuries were more severe than those sustained by her younger brother, Muhammad Adam Mohd Hardi, 8, after both children were buried under hot tar in the Nov 1 accident. Onn Hafiz also celebrated Hasya Fahira's birthday, which falls today.

items.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
items.summary: Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple climate funding for poorer countries to US$300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing from all public and private sources combined would be US$1.3 trillion annually. The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

items.title: One hour of rain, roads under water: Flash floods hit Shah Alam’s i-City
items.summary: A user, frhn.jefx, posted a video showing a flooded road near i-City, with several vehicles, particularly motorcycles, forced to stop along the stretch. Another user, jacketpotato.sa, also shared information on conditions along the same route, showing several cars making their way through the floodwaters. Another user, charlie.kilo.maggi, shared footage of flash flooding at 2.46pm along the exit from the i-City area.

items.title: Seats, candidates, strategy — Sarawak DAP will decide, says Loke
items.summary: KLUANG, Nov 15 — DAP has given full autonomy to the Sarawak DAP leadership to decide how many seats to contest, who to field and its strategy for the upcoming Sarawak state election, party secretary-general Anthony Loke said. “All decisions concerning the Sarawak state election will be made by Sarawak DAP. Asked about the party’s seat projections and the challenges it would face in the state election, Loke said details would be announced by the Sarawak DAP leadership at an appropriate time.

items.title: From setbacks to comeback? Dzulkefly wants Amanah ready for GE16
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 15 — Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) must use its defeats in several state elections as a springboard to strengthen the party and prepare its machinery for the 16th General Election (GE16), its vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said. He said the entire party leadership and machinery, particularly the youth and young women, must self-reflect, strengthen the organisation and devise more effective strategies for reaching out to the people. Dzulkefly said Amanah’s struggle should not be centred solely on electoral victory; rather, political victory must serve as a means to build a united, strong and dignified nation-state grounded in the values of human dignity (karamah insaniah).

items.title: Loke says Anwar need not bow to calls for early dissolution of Parliament
items.summary: KLUANG, Nov 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim need not bow to calls for an early dissolution of Parliament as long as he continues to command the support of a majority of Members of the Dewan Rakyat, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook. “As long as the Prime Minister commands the support of a majority in the Dewan Rakyat, there is no reason for him to bow to any pressure,” he said. “The Prime Minister should use this one-year period to carry out such work and reforms rather than bowing to pressure to dissolve Parliament,” he said.

items.title: Stormy evening ahead as MetMalaysia issues warning for multiple states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to hit parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak until 8pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). In an alert issued at 3.30pm, MetMalaysia said the affected areas in the peninsula include Perlis; Penang; and several districts in Kedah, Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Terengganu. In Perak, the districts affected are Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.

items.title: Anwar meets Carney in Manila, with Malaysia-Canada energy and digital trade on the table
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 15 — Efforts to expand trade and investment cooperation, particularly in the energy, digital economy and technology sectors, were among the key matters discussed during a meeting between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Canadian counterpart, Mark Carney, here. Anwar said the meeting, held on the sidelines of the 49th Asean Summit, also touched on bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments. “I also shared updates on Malaysia’s economic progress and explored potential new areas of collaboration, especially as we approach the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Malaysia and Canada.

items.title: Ab Rauf’s second-term to-do list: Economy, investments and fewer unanswered complaints
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 15 — The Melaka government will focus on strengthening the state’s economy, attracting investments and expediting the implementation of strategic development projects, while also improving the management of public complaints. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said all state development programmes would be implemented in an organised manner to ensure that the people benefit from them. “I do not want the people to wait too long to see the results of state development.

items.title: Fresh faces or familiar names? Abang Johari says GPS candidate list coming Nov 25
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 15 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will announce the full list of all 82 candidates who will contest in the 13th Sarawak state election on Nov 25, said its chairman, Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg. Earlier, Abang Johari hinted that eight incumbent State Legislative Assembly members from GPS might be retained as candidates involving four PBB representatives namely Fazzrudin Abdul Rahman, Datuk Ibrahim Baki, Datuk Hamzah Brahim, and Datuk Martin Ben. GPS comprises four component parties namely PBB, SUPP, Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS), and the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP).

items.title: Kedah Sultan gives nod to UUM’s RM15m Kedah Tua Museum plan
items.summary: His Royal Highness said the museum project would require an allocation of RM15 million, covering the construction of a new building, public exhibition areas, digital exhibition spaces, a conservation laboratory, artefact storage, research and management facilities. He said the museum would showcase the grandeur of the ancient Kedah civilisation for the appreciation of younger generations, including its governance, topography, history and the Sungai Batu civilisation. “The museum will also house various historical artefacts, including swords, iron ore, iron furnaces and a collection of currency,” he said.

items.title: ‘I’m CM for everyone’, says Ab Rauf as he calls for unity after Melaka polls, declares Nov 16 holiday
items.summary: MELAKA, 15 Nov — A day after the 16th Melaka State Election, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has called on the people of the state to unite as one big family, setting aside any differences in views or political affiliations that may have emerged during the election. I am the Chief Minister for all the people of Melaka, regardless of race, religion, background or political inclination,” he told reporters after taking his oath of office as the 13th Melaka Chief Minister, marking his second term, at the Office of the Yang Dipertua Negeri at Seri Negeri today. Meanwhile, Ab Rauf announced that tomorrow, Monday (Nov 16), would be a special public holiday in Melaka.

items.title: Anwar urges Asean to diversify food, medicine supply sources amid global uncertainty
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on Asean member states to diversify their sources of food and medicines while strengthening regional production capacity to reduce reliance on external suppliers amid growing global uncertainties. On medicines, Anwar urged Asean countries to recognise one another’s regulatory approvals, pool their purchasing power and stockpiles, and expand regional manufacturing of essential medicines and vaccines. On energy, Anwar said the Asean Power Grid (APG) remained the bloc’s foremost strategic priority.

items.title: Living alone, but not alone: AI pilot at Razak Mansion aims to spot falls and raise alarms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Elderly residents living alone at Razak Mansion could soon have an additional layer of protection through a new pilot project using artificial intelligence (AI), radar and thermal sensors to detect falls and unusual inactivity in their homes. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the initiative would explore how technology, particularly the Internet of Things (IoT), could be used to improve the safety and care of older adults as part of wider smart city efforts. Fahmi said the pilot would run around the clock for six months to assess the technology’s effectiveness, safety and sustainability, including whether its operating costs would make it practical for wider implementation.

items.title: After Melaka defeat, Fahmi says Pakatan will examine candidates, youth vote and turnout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will examine its candidates’ preparedness, youth voting patterns and lower voter turnout as part of a post-mortem following its disappointing performance in the Melaka state election. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the coalition would hold an initial meeting this week to assess the results and identify areas that need improvement ahead of future elections. He said one of the issues that needed to be examined was whether candidates were adequately prepared to contest their respective seats and carry out effective campaigns.

items.title: Fahmi wants stronger WhatsApp verification after scammers impersonate MCMC officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil wants WhatsApp to strengthen verification of phone numbers linked to its accounts amid growing concerns over scammers exploiting the messaging platform to deceive the public. He said the government was looking into the issue following reports of scammers misusing telephone numbers and WhatsApp accounts, including impersonating Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) officers. “So one thing that many countries are doing is to verify the identity and the telephone number that are linked to the WhatsApp account,” he said.

items.title: Sultan Nazrin confers Perak state honours on 24 recipients at birthday investiture
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Nov 15 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, today conferred state awards and medals of Perak on 24 recipients at Istana Iskandariah in conjunction with his 70th birthday. Also in attendance were the Raja Muda of Perak, Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, and Raja Di Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzurkarnain Sultan Idris Shah. Sultan Nazrin also conferred the Darjah Dato’ Seri Panglima Taming Sari (SPTS) upon Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, which carries the title “Datuk Seri Panglima”.
